brief: UBS expects the Fed to raise rates this week, a shift in the macro backdrop, but argues earnings growth stays the main driver of equity gains, so it retains S&P 500 targets of 8,100 for year-end and 8,400 for mid-2027. Across 16 hiking cycles since 1954, US equities never entered a bear market in the 12 months after the first hike and averaged a 10.8% gain, because ISM Manufacturing New Orders, not the hike itself, best explains post-hike equity returns; the 2022 cycle's -9% outcome coincided with New Orders collapsing from 60 to 46. Bond markets already price roughly four hikes over the next year, pushing the 10-year yield toward 5% and the S&P 500 forward P/E down to 19.5x from 22x, so UBS thinks most of the valuation adjustment has already happened. Because today's inflation overshoot is largely tariff- and energy-driven (temporary), and cumulative hikes of 1.5pp or less have historically implied low recession risk, UBS does not expect an aggressive hiking cycle. The bigger medium-term risk it flags is AI infrastructure investment, though it believes substantially more tightening would be needed before financing becomes a real constraint.
